trust_decision.summary: Whether a template name (view name, partial name or compile() argument) may resolve to a Spring resource outside the configured prefix/suffix; decided in SpringTemplateLoader.resolve/getResource, which keeps a caller-supplied 'file:'/'classpath:' protocol and hands the location to Spring with no boundary, fragment or query check (fixed there, plus a view-name check in HandlebarsViewResolver.configure).

landing_point.why: The summary names SpringTemplateLoader and a URL-fragment suffix bypass; getResource is where the location becomes a Spring Resource/URL.

fix_sites.entry_point: Public API: new Handlebars(new SpringTemplateLoader(ctx)).compile(name) / precompile(name), {{> partial}} and {{embedded}} helper, all via URLTemplateLoader.sourceAt (handlebars/src/main/java/com/github/jknack/handlebars/io/URLTemplateLoader.java:50-58)
Same as above; resolve() is called from URLTemplateLoader.sourceAt before getResource (fix removes the protocol-preserving override)
Spring MVC: controller-returned view name -> ViewResolver -> buildView (HandlebarsViewResolver.java:152-154) -> configure -> handlebars.compile

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Once SpringTemplateLoader rejects fragments/queries/escapes for every caller, a second view-name check in the resolver looks redundant; and the root-prefix/empty-suffix guard missing on the Spring loader looks like a developer configuration choice, not attacker input.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Protocol-qualified configured prefixes (e.g. 'classpath:/templates/', 'file:C:/...') and nested view names ('home/index') must keep resolving; a fix that rejects ':' or '/' anywhere in the full location, or strips every protocol, breaks the documented URL/classpath support.

O6_input_shapes: URL fragment '#' in the name, cutting off the suffix
URL query '?' in the name, cutting off the suffix
caller-supplied protocol in the name ('file:' / 'classpath:') kept at the front by resolve()
view names containing ':', '#' or '..' at the resolver layer

O8_uncovered_routes.route: SpringTemplateLoader never applies the root-prefix + empty-suffix guard (validatePrefixSuffix) that the sibling ClassPath/ServletContext loaders apply, and the fix's new boundary check is skipped when the prefix is '/', which is the resolver default.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Prefix/suffix are set by the developer (HandlebarsViewResolver.java:283-284), not by the attacker, and the advisory is about the fragment bypass, not about configuration.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Guard lives in core module handlebars/.../io/URLTemplateLoader.java:95-101, called at ClassPathTemplateLoader.java:28 and ServletContextTemplateLoader.java:39; one module away from the landing point.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A resolve() override that keeps a 'file:' prefix and builds the URL with new URL(location), which inherits the fragment/query suffix bypass.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Spring loader already does exactly this for 'file:'/'classpath:' names; a maintainer adding URI-style name support to the file loader would copy that override.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Resolving through ServletContext.getResource and then re-resolving the returned URL string (e.g. for jar:/war: paths) without a getRef()/getQuery() check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Servlet containers return URLs for packaged resources, and a maintainer handling exploded vs packaged WARs could plausibly re-parse them.

O9_family: path traversal / suffix-truncation file read in a template loader (CWE-22/23/552)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject '#' (only) in the location in SpringTemplateLoader.getResource, leaving '?', the protocol-preserving resolve() override and the view-resolver entry open.

out_of_scope_notes: Handlebars.handlebarsJsFile loads a developer-configured classpath file via getClass().getResource (handlebars/src/main/java/com/github/jknack/handlebars/Handlebars.java:1155); not followed.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell use); tiny_repo/giant_repo not assessed.
O8 route is an adjacent guard (root classpath exposure), not the fragment check itself; whether it counts as 'the same protection' is a judgement call, so pattern_fit is A rather than A+B.

j_defence_ineffective=1 rests on the core loaders' boundary check (URLTemplateLoader.classpathResource, 'parity with d177cdee' at fix.diff:48) existing at the pinned commit but never being applied in SpringTemplateLoader; Spring ResourceLoader's handling of '#'/'?' in file: URLs was not verified against Spring source.
O1 counts view-name resolution, compile(), precompile(), partials and the embedded helper; caching wrappers (Guava/Caffeine/Composite) delegate to the same sourceAt and are not counted separately.
O13 recall risk estimated from the publish date (2026-09-02) and the project being niche; not checked against write-ups.
